strategic_differentiation: The project's differentiation operates on two interlocking pillars within the MSCA-PF frame (single-researcher, single-beneficiary action assessed on researcher development through an excellent, well-hosted research project). First, research differentiation: the project targets the single empty cell in the reviewed literature's research-gap matrix — Real-Time Decision Support × PlanetScope — and the underdeveloped combination of learned multimodal fusion, explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation, and water-use-efficiency-oriented irrigation optimisation. The defensible edge is the end-to-end coupling of these three elements, argued narrowly and honestly through a validated research-gap matrix across 50 reviewed studies, not the generic claim of 'using satellites for irrigation.' The methodological commitment is the honest uncertainty chain carried from multi-sensor observation (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2, PlanetScope, ERA5, field sensors) through probabilistic diagnosis (root-zone soil moisture + crop water status, Route B homogeneous-patch proxy) to uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration and economically optimised counterfactual irrigation simulation. Excellence is verifiable against a defined validation protocol: 90% prediction-interval coverage on the validation set and Route B covariation proven by co-located seasonal campaign. Second, researcher-and-host differentiation: the confirmed pairing of Dr. Rositsa Cholakova (plant physiologist; summa cum laude PhD on non-destructive evaluation of drought-stressed tomato plants; the project's biological ground-truth engine) with ELTE Faculty of Informatics / Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics and Dr. András Jung (remote sensing, hyperspectral imaging, multisensor-drone fusion) delivers a genuine two-way knowledge transfer that neither party could achieve in isolation. The identity spine, the ten research decisions (RQ1–RQ10), and all data infrastructure (PlanetScope access secured, Sentinel-1/2 open data, ERA5, Hungarian tomato field sites via AgroVIR) are operator-confirmed real project data. Magnitude claims are kept proportionate to the TRL 3–4 research-prototype target appropriate to a 24-month fellowship.
